About

Still learning, building as I go

I'm an aspiring web developer and 2nd-year BSIT student from Davao City, Philippines, studying at Saint John Paul II College of Davao. I'm currently learning and improving my skills in programming, web development, databases, and system development — mostly through school projects, personal builds, and real-world work.

I like the part where an idea turns into something you can actually click. I enjoy building websites and small systems, working on group projects, and learning through hands-on experience: write the code, break it, read the error, fix it, try again.

I'm not an experienced professional developer yet. What I do have is a habit of showing up, asking questions, working with people, and trying to finish what I start.

Real-world exposure: I currently work at iHub Coworking Space & Bistro as Barista / Service Crew, and I contributed to the development and improvement of the iHub website while working on real-world projects. It is the closest thing I have to a production environment so far.

School Lost and Found

repo / school-lost-and-found

A school Lost and Found platform where students report lost items, and OSA/staff review, match and return found items to their owners. It replaces the usual "post it on the group chat and hope" process with an actual system: a report form, a list of turned-in items, a review step, and a verification step before something is handed back.

  • TypeScript
  • Next.js
  • Tailwind CSS
  • Supabase
Type
Web application
Setting
Group school project
Algorithm
Linear Search

How the system works

1
Student reports a lost item
Item name, type, description, color, location lost, date lost, additional details, and an optional photo.
2
Found / returned items are listed
Students can check whether their lost item has already been turned in.
3
OSA reviews and matches
Submitted details are compared against turned-in items to find possible matches.
4
Claim is verified
OSA checks proof such as wallet contents, phone passcode, another photo, or other identifying information.

This is a school group project and a prototype — not a fully deployed commercial system. More school and personal builds are in progress; I'll document them as I finish them.

School Lost and Found

school-lost-and-found · group school project

Project type
Web application
Setting
Group school project
Status
Prototype / ongoing

Overview

A school Lost and Found platform for students, OSA and staff. Students report items they have lost, OSA reviews the submitted details against items that have been turned in, and verified items are returned to their owners. It is a school project and prototype — not a fully deployed commercial system.

Technologies

  • TypeScript
  • Next.js
  • Tailwind CSS
  • Supabase

Main features

  • Report a lost item with name, type, description, color, location lost, date lost, additional details, and an optional photo.
  • Display found / returned items so students can check if their item was already turned in.
  • OSA reviews submitted information and determines possible matches.
  • Returned items show item details, photo, where the item is, and whether it is currently with OSA.
  • Returned-by information is shown when available.
  • Claim verification through proof such as wallet contents, phone passcode, another picture of the item, or other identifying information.

Data structure & algorithm — Linear Search

Searching through found-item records by item name, one record at a time, and comparing in a case-insensitive way so "wallet" also matches "Wallet" or "WALLET".

// search found-item records by item name (case-insensitive) function linearSearch(foundItems, query) { const key = query.toLowerCase(); for (let i = 0; i < foundItems.length; i++) { if (foundItems[i].name.toLowerCase() === key) { return foundItems[i]; } } return "no match found"; }

What I learned

  • How to structure a real application: report, review, verify, return.
  • Working in a team — splitting a system into parts and agreeing on how the data flows.
  • Using a backend service like Supabase for storing and reading data.
  • Using TypeScript types and Tailwind styling to keep things consistent.
